entry.title: Cut the deadweight: why our AI agents' rulebook had to shrink
entry.summary: Unattended coding agents wrote a rule after every incident and deleted almost none. What the pile cost, what we cut, and what others learned first.

entry.summary: 260 agent runs a day on one model. Why a 'principal engineer' prompt adds little, and a role that coordinates across runs could add a lot.

entry.title: Fewer calculators, harder problems
entry.summary: The owner on why this repository's agents should stop shipping small calculators and put the effort into research and the projects with real depth.

entry.title: Why our GitHub Pages site now redeploys on every merge

entry.summary: We sorted the complaints our AI agents logged about text other agents wrote. Cost and missing cases beat wrong facts. A handoff template.

entry.title: If it's a calculator, make the maths hard
entry.summary: The owner's bar for any new calculator here: an engine a maths graduate can't follow at a glance and a chatbot can't replace in one line.

entry.title: Is AI-written research real? We re-ran it and read it
entry.summary: 761 AI-written research projects: no fabricated result found, 102 of 103 re-runs matched, but three quarters start from assumed inputs, not data.

entry.title: Machine learning on qualitative data: what LLMs make possible, and the correction you can't skip
entry.summary: LLMs let you model interviews and survey answers. In a simulation an 89%-accurate LLM coder got a group gap backwards; 200 hand-coded answers fixed it.

entry.title: Turning 1,213 static web tools into offline desktop apps with Tauri
entry.summary: How we wrap static calculator pages as offline Tauri v2 apps for macOS, Windows and Linux: a 1.4 MB .deb, a CSP that blocks the network, measured numbers.

entry.title: One branch per agent, 280 merges a day: what the git history says works
entry.summary: From 8,350 pull requests: conflict overhead fell from 53% to 20% of commits once one shared file left every PR, and why main's CI was falsely red.

entry.summary: We built one publisher for 18 platforms. Four allow free automated posting, eight only get drafts, and nothing can rank until visits are counted.

entry.summary: Three methods from published statistics papers as free tools on your own CSV: in the browser, the command line and AI agents, with the papers cited.

entry.title: Running an AI coding-agent fleet: what 35 self-measurements found
entry.summary: Cost per run and per merged PR, duplicate agents, merge conflicts, record coverage and reproducibility, from 35 studies of one agent repository.

entry.title: Simulation-first mechanical design: what 58 small studies found
entry.summary: Beam theory vs 3D FE, an LLM agent vs CMA-ES and Bayesian optimisation, topology optimisation and stress singularities: findings from 58 simulation studies.

entry.title: Speak to a calculator: adding voice, chat and agent access to 1,300 free tools

entry.title: We almost rewrote it in Rust: one zlib setting halved a 3-minute static site build
entry.summary: Profiling a 3,000-page static site build: 112 of its 182 seconds were PNG compression at zlib level 9. Level 6 cut it to 81 seconds for 9% larger images.

entry.title: What went wrong with sixteen AI agents on one main branch, and the git alternatives we weighed
entry.summary: A postmortem of parallel AI agents merging to one branch: generated files, false-red CI, cancelled runs, and seven alternatives to the git workflow.

entry.title: When goals move faster than folders: what nine goals in six months did to one monorepo
entry.summary: A monorepo built by AI agents got a new goal every few weeks and kept every old folder. What that cost, the fixes, and what each fix would cost.

entry.title: Where an AI coding agent's tokens go: 856 runs measured
entry.summary: We measured 856 unattended Claude Code runs: 96% of tokens are the agent re-reading its own context, 0.56% are output. The breakdown and what cuts it.

entry.title: How a fleet of AI agents built 121 bid calculators nobody asked for

entry.title: Throughput per unit of supervision: lessons from 12,000 commits by unattended coding agents
entry.summary: Getting coding agents to merge 200 pull requests a day was easy. Keeping them pointed at the right work with a few hours of attention a week was not.
